title: Al Viola and the postponed Jay McShann concert
summary: On 18 May 1982 Callender adds guitarist Al Viola to the concert list and talks about looking forward to playing with McShann.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Before we go any further, I would like to go back to March 5th. I left out one guy, one of the most important ones, Al Viola, who played a wonderful rendition of "Send In The Clowns" on his beautiful Classical guitar. It was another highlight of our performance.
It certainly was. I was very, very impressed.
I wouldn't want to leave that out.
You were telling me about the performance with Jay McShann that you mentioned last week.

Yes. I mentioned last week that we were to play on the 3rd of June, but it's since been cancelled because the school didn't think it would be fair to have him compete against Benny Goodman and Ella Fitzgerald and Sarah Vaughan on the same day -- and I think they're right. So most likely they will try to reschedule it at a later date.

I hope so. I've been looking forward to playing with Jay McShann. When I told Gerry Wiggins I was going to work with Jay McShann, he said, 'oh, wonderful; he's the last of the Kansas City greats of that Basie period.'
Have you ever worked with Jay McShann before?

No, I've never worked with him before. I've heard the band, you know. Charlie Parker used to play in his band! So yeah, I know all about Jay McShann, but I've never had the pleasure. I'm looking forward to it.
